paraphrase: The Veda is that text which makes known the supernatural means (alaukika upāya) of obtaining the desired and avoiding the undesired; it is authoritative in itself, being authorless.
notes: Paraphrase of the definition in Sāyaṇa's introductions (recalled; the same definition appears in his introduction to the Taittirīya Saṃhitā). Locator 'upodghāta' is chapter-level.

queries: Sāyaṇa definition Veda iṣṭaprāptyaniṣṭaparihārayoḥ alaukikam upāyam Taittirīya Saṃhitā bhāṣya upodghāta

checks.note: Web sources confirm the definition (the Veda reveals the supra-mundane means of obtaining the desired and avoiding the undesired) in Sāyaṇa's upodghāta to the Taittirīya Saṃhitā, and confirm that his Ṛgveda introduction (Ṛgbhāṣyabhūmikā) argues the Veda's authorlessness (apauruṣeyatva) and self-validity. The exact wording of the definition inside the Ṛgveda upodghāta itself was not seen (the local Sāyaṇa files are verse commentaries without the upodghāta); the locator is chapter-level as the entry says.
